method.method_draft: Use a counting-by-intervals argument relative to the given 5 and 7. From the image, the arrows show 7 points upward to the top-left square and then rightward to the top-middle square, so two squares must be greater than 7. Since the only numbers greater than 7 among 1 to 9 are 8 and 9, those two squares consume both 8 and 9. Separately, the bottom-middle square points into the 5, the center points down to the bottom-middle, the bottom-right points left to the bottom-middle, and the middle-right points down toward the bottom-right, so four distinct squares are forced to be less than 5. The only four numbers less than 5 are 1,2,3,4, so those four squares consume all numbers below 5. The question-mark square is not one of the given 5 or 7, cannot use any number below 5, and cannot use 8 or 9; therefore the only possible remaining value is 6.
